# AI Engineering Compiler v0.2.0

The trust release. If you used 0.1.x, read the two fixes first — both changed
what lands in your repository.

## Your files are safe now

`aie sync` in 0.1 deleted the entire runtime directory before regenerating it,
which destroyed a pre-existing `.claude/settings.json` on the first run.

Every target now records the files it owns in `.ai/state/targets/<id>.json`
(committed alongside your generated files). A file is only removed or
overwritten when that record lists it, when its bytes still match the source it
was copied from, or when it carries the generated banner. Everything else is a
collision: sync reports every colliding path and stops before writing.

## Output lands where the runtimes read it

0.1 wrote `AGENTS.md` inside `.codex/`, which Codex never loads, and never
generated a root `CLAUDE.md` at all. Both are now generated at the repository
root, and `.codex/` is no longer created.

## Already have instruction files? Import them

```sh
npx aie adopt
```

Splits your existing `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/agents/`,
`.cursor/rules/`, and Copilot instructions into `.ai/` sources. Dry run by
default, never modifies the originals, and flags pairs that look like the same
policy written twice — usually the first time that drift is visible at all.

## Hooks, Cursor, and workflows

- **Hooks compile.** Declare one with a normalized event and a script; the
  Claude adapter wires it into `.claude/settings.json` and owns only the entries
  it wrote. Your permissions and your own hooks are preserved, and an entry you
  edit by hand is reported instead of overwritten.
- **Cursor is a third runtime.** Rules become `.cursor/rules/*.mdc`, with
  `scope:` frontmatter compiling to Cursor's `globs`.
- **Workflow blueprints.** `aie init --blueprint` writes a `.ai/blueprint.yaml`
  that names an engineering workflow instead of listing files. `aie sync`
  composes a versioned pack into a committed `.ai/generated/`, and `aie explain`
  shows what came from where. One workflow ships: `spec-driven`.

## Also in this release

- `aie check` — drift detection that writes nothing. Exit 0 clean, 1 out of
  date, 2 broken workspace. Replaces `sync && git diff --exit-code` in CI.
- A GitHub Action that runs it and annotates the drifted files on the PR.
- Both targets compile the same set of sources; they could previously disagree.
- `aie init` seeds a rule and working templates, so the first sync produces real
  instructions rather than an empty file.
- Diagnostics with stable codes for everything that is skipped, unsupported, or
  deprecated. Nothing is dropped silently.
- `commands` sources compile to `.claude/commands/`.
- `--strict`, `--force`, `--write`, `--blueprint`, `--dry-run`, and `--json`.

## Breaking

- The `ai` command is now `aie`. `ai` still works with a deprecation warning and
  will be removed in 0.3.0.
- Adapters must return `{ files: [{ path, contents }] }` from `render` and must
  not write to disk.
- Rules are inlined into `CLAUDE.md` instead of copied to `.claude/rules/`.
- `.ai/hooks/` is no longer copied; hook compilation is not implemented, and
  pretending otherwise registered nothing.

## Upgrading

Run `aie sync`. Unchanged generated files are adopted silently; a hand-written
`CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md` is reported so you can move it aside or run
`aie sync --force` after checking the diff.
